description: REQ-117's own step 6 text reads: 'invokes `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId, borrowerId, nowMs})` (REQ-115) EXACTLY ONCE this wake' -- a call with exactly ONE argument. But the REAL, current, already-converged (sprint-2) `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt` in `~/anicca/skills/economy/lending/lib/lending-orchestrator.mjs:268` has signature `({ lenderId, borrowerId, nowMs = Date.now() } = {}, deps = {})` -- a SECOND, separate `deps` parameter -- and its own body reads `const getCitizen = deps.getCitizen;` (line 276) with NO fallback default (unlike `ledgerFile`/`lockStatePath`/`gojoLogRows`, which all use `deps.x || <real default>`). `getCitizen` is then called unconditionally at line 280 (`getCitizen(lenderId)`) and again inside `runLockedIssuance` at line 191 (the REQ-106 'fresh recheck... never the pre-lock snapshot' step). Empirically verified this review (fresh execution, not merely static reading): calling the REAL, unmodified `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId:'a', borrowerId:'b', nowMs: Date.now()})` with no second argument -- EXACTLY as REQ-117's own step-6 text literally shows it being invoked -- throws `TypeError: getCitizen is not a function` immediately, before any eligibility/sizing/disbursement logic ever runs. REQ-117's own text never once mentions `getCitizen`, `deps`, or any second argument to this call anywhere in its step 6, its Dependencies discussion, its Edge Cases, or its Acceptance Criteria -- confirmed by a full-text grep of both `specs/behavioral-spec.md` and `specs/verification-architecture.md` for `getCitizen`, which returns zero matches in either file. This is not a stylistic omission: it means REQ-117, exactly as currently specified, describes an entry point that would throw an uncaught exception on EVERY real wake where step 5 actually selects a candidate pair -- the single scenario this REQ's own EARS clause exists to make possible ('THE SYSTEM SHALL make REQ-115's `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt`... genuinely INVOKED'). The exception would propagate out of `runWakeGate` to the CLI entrypoint's own top-level `.catch()` (per REQ-117's own, now-corrected, step-9 exit-code text), meaning the ONE real, deliberate, successful loan-issuance path this whole feature exists to reach would ALWAYS present to any exit-code-watching monitor as a genuine daemon failure, indistinguishable from a real bug -- the exact failure mode REQ-117's own step-9 correction (FIND-1001's fix) just finished explaining must be avoided for a routine REFUSAL, yet here it would happen for the SUCCESS path instead. This also makes PROP-117c's own THIRD fixture (two qualifying citizens -> `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt` invoked with the correct pair) unimplementable against the REAL, unmodified function as REQ-117 currently specifies the call: the call would throw before producing any of the `{status: 'active'|'disbursement_failed'|...}` outcomes PROP-117c's own fixture needs to observe. Secondarily (same root cause, lower severity): `runLockedIssuance` also reads `deps.gojoLogRows` (line 179/216, DOES have a safe fallback default of `[]` at line 277, so this half does not crash) to compute `sumRecentGojoGiftsUsd` inside the SAME fresh-recheck sizing step -- if REQ-117's step 6 call also fails to thread step 3's already-read `gojoLogRows` through, the disbursement recheck would silently and incorrectly treat ANY recently-received gojo gift as $0 every real wake, a silent correctness bug distinct from (but touching the same unspecified-deps gap as) the `getCitizen` crash.
